Replay

Dedicated Scrapyard comparison

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

build.sh OUTPUT creates separate old/new projects, preserving the sibling Scrapyard checkout. execute.py OUTPUT LABEL runs a dedicated authority and two clients in each build; report.py OUTPUT LABEL validates the paired receipts.

The scenario follows the original server act: clients join and Ready, clear a six-enemy wave, receive their core, and regroup to advance to floor two without an authority avatar or a player-host Start command. Both implementations use the same circle-strafe/autofire and south-lane controller. The original launcher’s one-wave/no-barrel, 255-magazine/no-jam overrides are retained; both clients explicitly choose the bolter. Receive delay is 120 ms per process and simulation runs at 60 Hz. No HP, position, damage, kill or progression state is edited.

The baseline copy uses the existing declared ownership-cleanup overlay. Gameplay sources and the original launcher are preserved. Prepared file hashes, framework hashes, binary identities, actual driver, environment and actor traces accompany results. Original run.sh is not executed because it deletes baseline profiles.

This gate proves that the named dedicated-server act works in both implementations. It does not establish matching movement streams, damage distribution, elapsed combat times, broader mode parity or a performance advantage. Kit's client player IDs are 2/3 because its authority identity is reserved; Replay's playable seats are 1/2. Those IDs also affect authored spawn positions. The comparison records these boundaries rather than treating one run as full gameplay equivalence.
